reviews.review: this game feels like watching a t-rex on a monster truck while he's sipping beer and shooting monsters with light machine guns
Runs like #2 sometimes, but it is a fun game and they've been fixing a lot of the performance issues lately.

Devs are being quite tone deaf recently patch after patch, and they're doing blanket balance changes instead of specifically adjusting the problem stratagem they want to adjust which is leading to some residual issues that they have to fix later. Balance debt after balance debt because they can't be asked to step up and do playtesting or adjust the numbers of the bastion or mech instead of just boosting all the numbers higher one at a time...

All this balance debt adds up and means they have less and less time to fix game-breaking bugs like a terminal bug that's been in the game since launch, but they will happily step forward to fix a bug that favors the player within a day.

On top of that they just keep making promises about enemy design, or promises in general, and breaking them. I for one am just getting tired of it, boss, I love this game even now but they need to start changing their approach for the longevity of the game. People are so divided right now and it's to the point one side is telling the other to just straight up leave, but people leave when they encounter ♥♥♥♥... this game has potential, it was and can continue to be fun; so people are giving it criticism. The criticism is only as harsh as it is because expectations are continuously not met, and they keep making the same mistakes time in and time out. People don't want to leave because they have hope the game will become less ♥♥♥♥, but if they keep this path and people keep pushing others out for not liking the direction, this game will start dying and fading into obscurity as other studios fill the gap.

Now they release a new update that breaks the game on an entire OS, ♥♥♥♥♥ it on the steam deck, and even messes it up for some people whom had perfectly fine experiences before as now the game simply errors instead of letting them launch in. Hardware parity will always be an issue but to this extent is frankly absurd, and it goes to show just how little they actually QA test anything. Furthermore, in a recent interview they said that it's up to the *players* to test things now that they've released things, and overall they are continuously condescending in communications while only taking criticism from the most censored sources because they can't take what they give and can't tolerate when people are upset when they break promises. It's a really sad state of affairs and it's not fair for either side for how bad it's gotten, but it's only gotten this bad due to the sincere neglect of duty on the part of the devs. All of these issues and yet they still push warbond after warbond instead of creating non-freemium content or progression, and even went as far as to say that most things the general community has been asking for is not a priority right now.

I'll likely still bash my head against this brick wall to play Helldivers 2, but I don't think I can recommend it in its current monkey paw balancing state. I hope they make their direction clearer in the future with better patch notes, and I hope they stop making technical debt for themselves in the future. Game dev isn't as simple as people are making it out to be but the numbers tweaks they're providing shouldn't take so long to change and balance test.

The AMA was a step in the right direction, but their patches will speak louder than words until they can earn community trust back enough.
